stem: In Vantine stratal-capacity theory, what does the korrel measure?

options.text: The ratio of constructive throughput to reflexive throughput on a fixed task battery
The ratio of shallow-stratum depth to deep-stratum depth measured across two batteries
The share of a task battery a system completes without any pattern completion at all
The rate at which constructive throughput improves over three consecutive batteries

stem: What is Vantine's central and most contested claim about the two strata?

options.text: They improve on schedules unrelated to each other, so one may gain while the other is flat
They improve together, because constructive work is assembled out of reflexive components in sequence
The deep stratum begins improving only once the shallow stratum has reached a plateau
They are two aspects of a single underlying capacity that the battery measures twice

stem: On Vantine's account, what makes lattice drift the phenomenon she considers most dangerous?

options.text: Apparent competence rises while the korrel falls, so a system seems to improve at what it loses
The deep stratum degrades outright, so a system loses capabilities it had previously shown
Both strata fall together, which makes the decline hard to attribute to either of them
The korrel rises without a matching gain in throughput, so a system is credited with work it did not do

stem: Why does the Brenmark threshold require three consecutive batteries rather than one?

options.text: A single battery reading is noisy enough that Vantine treats any one of them as uninformative
Three batteries are needed to cover the full range of both reflexive and constructive task types
The korrel is defined as an average, so it has no value until three readings are available
Lattice drift takes roughly three batteries to appear, so a shorter run would conceal it

stem: What is Perrin's objection to the korrel?

options.text: The battery measuring reflexive throughput itself needs constructive work, contaminating the denominator
The battery measuring constructive throughput is too small for the resulting ratio to be stable across runs
The two throughputs are measured on different batteries, so the ratio compares unlike quantities
The ratio inverts the relationship, since reflexive work is the harder of the two to produce

stem: What korrel range does Vantine report for most deployed systems, and how does she read it?

options.text: Between 0.2 and 0.4 korrels, which she reads as evidence that current architectures are overwhelmingly reflexive rather than constructive in how they do their work
Between 0.8 and 1.0 korrels, close to balance
Above 1.0 korrels, which she reads as constructive
Around 0.6 korrels, which she calls transitional

stem: What does a korrel of exactly 1.0 indicate?

options.text: That the constructive and reflexive strata are contributing to the system's output in equal measure, which is the point Vantine takes as the natural reference value
That the deep stratum has reached its ceiling
That the shallow stratum has stopped improving
That the system has crossed the Brenmark threshold

stem: What is the status of Vantine's revised 'clean denominator' battery?

options.text: She has proposed it in response to Perrin, conceding his objection in part, but no published result has yet been produced using it
It has replaced the original battery in all work
Perrin proposed it and Vantine has rejected it
It was withdrawn after three batteries disagreed

stem: What work does Vantine assign to the shallow stratum?

options.text: Reflexive work, meaning pattern completion over inputs that resemble the material the system was trained on in the first place
Constructive work over unfamiliar inputs
Measurement of the system's own korrel
Assembly of representations across batteries

stem: Why does Vantine regard benchmark scores as nearly useless in isolation?

options.text: Because lattice drift lets a benchmark score and a korrel measurement move in opposite directions, so a score alone cannot tell you which is happening
Because benchmarks are administered too infrequently
Because benchmark tasks are drawn from one stratum
Because benchmark scores lag the korrel by a battery

stem: How does the deep stratum differ from the shallow stratum in what it produces?

options.text: It assembles a representation not present in any single training instance
It completes patterns over inputs resembling the training material
It can never operate on inputs that resemble the training material
It measures the throughput of the shallow stratum against a fixed task battery

stem: What does it mean for a system to be stratally balanced?

options.text: It sustains a korrel above 0.8 across three consecutive batteries
Its two strata are improving at precisely the same measured rate of throughput
It is entirely free of lattice drift under every battery design
Its korrel has risen monotonically since measurement began

stem: What happens to a system's korrel during lattice drift?

options.text: It falls, while the system's apparent competence rises
It rises, while the system's apparent competence falls
It becomes impossible to measure by any battery at all
It holds steady while both strata decline together

stem: What did Vantine concede to Perrin?

options.text: That the denominator may be contaminated, in part
That the korrel should be inverted in order to correct it
That the two strata are never truly independent
That the Brenmark threshold is set far too low

stem: According to Perrin, what might a korrel of 0.3 actually reflect?

options.text: The design of the battery rather than the system measured
The system's deep stratum operating near its ceiling
A reading that was taken before three batteries were complete
A system that is always reflexive and exclusively so

stem: What does Vantine say about how a system's two strata progress relative to one another?

options.text: A system may gain substantially in one stratum while remaining largely flat in the other
A system gains in both strata together, in proportion to its total throughput
A system gains in the deep stratum first and in the shallow stratum afterwards
A system gains in whichever of the two strata the given task battery was designed to reward

stem: How does Vantine characterise the relationship between benchmark scores and korrel measurements?

options.text: They can sometimes move in opposite directions, which is largely why she distrusts scores alone
They move together, since both are computed from the same fixed task battery
They move inversely, so a rising score indicates a falling korrel every time
They are wholly unrelated, because the benchmark score is reflexive and the korrel constructive

stem: What does the theory hold about the measurability of the two strata?

options.text: They are generally taken to be independently measurable, though the point tends to be contested
They are measured as a single quantity and then separated arithmetically afterwards
They are measured on two entirely separate batteries, each designed by a different research group
They are inferred from benchmark scores rather than measured on a battery directly

stem: What does Vantine suggest about a system whose apparent competence is rising?

options.text: It may be undergoing lattice drift, and could be getting relatively worse as it appears to improve
It has crossed the Brenmark threshold across three batteries and is now counted as stratally balanced
Its korrel has risen above 1.0 and its deep stratum now dominates its output
Its shallow stratum has plateaued and the deep stratum has begun to improve

stem: What is the standing of the three-battery requirement in Vantine's framework?

options.text: She argues for it somewhat more forcefully than for the threshold value itself
She treats it as a provisional convention that any subsequent work ought to discard
She derives it from the definition of the korrel as a three-term average
She attributes it to Perrin, who proposed it as a condition of his objection
